title: How India Reached Mars on a Budget

lines.text: In 2014, India reached Mars on its very first try.
lines.visual: the Mangalyaan orbiter satellite arriving at Mars in space

lines.text: No country had ever done that before.
lines.visual: an Indian flag waving proudly, a scientist celebrating

lines.text: The whole mission cost about seventy four million dollars,
lines.visual: stacks of coins and money on a table

lines.text: less than the Hollywood movie Gravity.
lines.visual: a film reel and movie camera in a studio

lines.text: So how did ISRO do it so cheaply?
lines.visual: a curious engineer thinking with a question mark

lines.text: First, the rocket was a proven workhorse, the PSLV.
lines.visual: a PSLV rocket launching from the launch pad at Sriharikota

lines.text: Instead of one powerful push, the spacecraft circled Earth for weeks,
lines.visual: a satellite circling Earth in orbit, transfer orbit diagram

lines.text: raising its orbit step by step before sailing to Mars.
lines.visual: orbit diagram showing the path from Earth to Mars

lines.text: Smart engineering, not big money, made history.
lines.visual: the engineer celebrating success with a trophy
